target.title: Drop redundant escaping in redirect
target.description: The location is already URL-encoded with iri_to_uri when the Location header is set, so escaping it again for the HTML body is redundant.

summary: Remove redundant escaping of the location string in the HTML body of redirect responses.

suspects.title: Unescaped location in HTML body could lead to XSS
suspects.problem: Removing escape(location) means that if the Location header contains characters like quotes or angle brackets (even if URL encoded, or if iri_to_uri does not encode certain characters like single quotes depending on version/context), injecting raw location values into the HTML attribute href="..." could result in XSS.
suspects.how_to_check: Check how iri_to_uri behaves with malicious inputs, and whether other places in the codebase escape URL strings before putting them into HTML attribute contexts.

arguments.claim: Removing escape(location) from the HTML body in redirect() allows unescaped location values to be rendered inside an href attribute, leading to XSS if a malicious location string containing quotes or angle brackets is passed.
arguments.suggested_fix: Restore html_location = escape(location) or use appropriate HTML escaping for the href and link text.

evidence.note: The location is directly interpolated into an HTML href attribute without escaping
html_location was changed from escape(location) to location

arguments.explanation: In src/werkzeug/utils.py, the redirect() function creates an HTML response page containing a clickable link with the target URL: `{html_location}`. Removing `escape(location)` means that characters like quotes (`"`) or angle brackets (`<`, `>`) in the `location` string are no longer escaped before being placed into the HTML attribute context. An attacker controlling or influencing the redirect location could inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript, resulting in XSS.
